item.title: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.dc:creator: Samir Abu-Rumeileh
Henning Großkopf
Arthur Guthknecht
Alexander Mensch
Dirk Osterloh
Antonia Ratti
Julian Conrad
Caroline Stapf
item.description:
Authors: Samir Abu-Rumeileh, Henning Großkopf, Arthur Guthknecht, Alexander Mensch, Dirk Osterloh, Antonia Ratti, Julian Conrad, Caroline Stapf, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10745
Abstract: Abstract Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS ( n = 139), AD ( n = 101) and controls ( n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain ( n = 16), spinal cord ( n = 11) and muscle ( n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

item.title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
item.dc:creator: Junghyun Lim
Marijana Vujkovic
Michael G. Levin
Kim Lorenz
Benjamin F. Voight
David Y. Zhang
Max. F. Dudek

item.description:
Authors: Junghyun Lim, Marijana Vujkovic, Michael G. Levin, Kim Lorenz, Benjamin F. Voight, David Y. Zhang, Max. F. Dudek, Matthew C. Pahl, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

item.title: Reduced-DSP 200G/λ low-voltage slow-light silicon modulator enabled by built-in EO equalizer
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Kawahara
Tai Tsuchizawa
Noritsugu Yamamoto
Yuriko Maegami
Koji Yamada
Nobuhiko Nishiyama
Toshihiko Baba
item.description:
Authors: Keisuke Kawahara, Tai Tsuchizawa, Noritsugu Yamamoto, Yuriko Maegami, Koji Yamada, Nobuhiko Nishiyama, Toshihiko Baba
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10446
Abstract: Abstract Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

item.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
item.dc:creator: Stefan Braunshier
Elda Cannavo
Vincent Morin
Sriram KK
Ananya Acharya
Giordano Reginato
Florian Morati
Virginie Ropars
item.description:
Authors: Stefan Braunshier, Elda Cannavo, Vincent Morin, Sriram KK, Ananya Acharya, Giordano Reginato, Florian Morati, Virginie Ropars, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired by Ku-dependent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) or DNA end resection-dependent homologous recombination (HR). Previously, it was shown that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 can remove Ku from DSBs and initiate resection, showing flexibility in DSB repair pathway choice. However, which NHEJ intermediates can be disrupted by resection factors remains unknown. Using reconstituted reactions with purified S. cerevisiae proteins, we show here that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 is not directly inhibited by any of the core NHEJ factors. Instead, we find that MRX-pSae2 is inhibited structurally. DNA synapsis, a dynamic NHEJ intermediate that bridges DSBs, strongly suppresses resection. Non-ligatable ends are refractory to MRX-pSae2 once synapsis formed, and NHEJ assemblies with catalytic mutants of DNA ligase IV that permit synapsis but do not allow ligation likewise inhibit resection. We further demonstrate that removal of Ku from DSBs requires RPA, which interacts with MRX and pSae2 to synergistically stimulate MRX 3′−5′ exonuclease activity, generating free 3′ overhangs. Our data support a model in which DNA synapsis temporarily prevents resection, allowing NHEJ to execute ligation. If ligation fails and synapsis dissociates, MRX-pSae2 and RPA promote resection that removes non-productive NHEJ assemblies and channels DSB repair toward HR. The data help explain the suppression of NHEJ by RPA observed in previous genetic experiments.

item.title: Laser-enhanced quantum sensing boosts sensitivity and dynamic range
item.dc:creator: Florian Schall
Lukas Lindner
Yves Rottstaedt
Marcel Rattunde
Florentin Reiter
Rüdiger Quay
Roman Bek
Alexander M. Zaitsev
item.description:
Authors: Florian Schall, Lukas Lindner, Yves Rottstaedt, Marcel Rattunde, Florentin Reiter, Rüdiger Quay, Roman Bek, Alexander M. Zaitsev, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10825
Abstract: Abstract While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. Here, we demonstrate a laser threshold magnetometry-based NV system that achieves 100% optical contrast in combination with strong output signals up to 50 mW. By integrating the NV centers into a laser cavity, we show magnetic-field-dependent shifts of the laser threshold, allowing the laser system to be entirely switched off with the NV centers’ magnetic resonance. We determine the photon-shot-noise fundamental sensitivity limit to be < 400 fT/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz for all vector components and demonstrate that it improves super-linearly with contrast. This sensitivity is not achieved at the usual cost of smaller linewidth, i.e., maintains good intrinsic dynamic range. This provides a perspective for highly sensitive magnetometry operated outside magnetically-shielded rooms for applications including magnetoencephalography, magnetic navigation, and magnetic anomaly detection.

item.title: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
item.dc:creator: Amitesh Panda
Léo Carrillo
Bradley Philip Balaton
Jeanne Brouillet
Solomon Nshemereirwe
Jarne Bonroy
Charbel Alfeghaly
Romina Facchinello
item.description:
Authors: Amitesh Panda, Léo Carrillo, Bradley Philip Balaton, Jeanne Brouillet, Solomon Nshemereirwe, Jarne Bonroy, Charbel Alfeghaly, Romina Facchinello, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10738
Abstract: Abstract X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

item.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
item.dc:creator: Ashley J. Newton
Adefoluke E. Kuforiji
Philipp A. M. Schmidpeter
item.description:
Authors: Ashley J. Newton, Adefoluke E. Kuforiji, Philipp A. M. Schmidpeter
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

item.title: High-content morphological profiling by Cell Painting in 3D spheroids
item.dc:creator: Christa Ringers
David Holmberg
Anders Larsson
Bomi Jung
Malin Jarvius
Anna Luchniak
Dan Rosén
Martin Johansson
item.description:
Authors: Christa Ringers, David Holmberg, Anders Larsson, Bomi Jung, Malin Jarvius, Anna Luchniak, Dan Rosén, Martin Johansson, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10790
Abstract: Abstract Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models – especially for studying drug perturbations – they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures’ interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

item.title: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization
item.dc:creator: José A. Martina
Akriti Prashar
Ana M. Pasapera
Katie Rollins
Eutteum Jeong
Rosa Puertollano
item.description:
Authors: José A. Martina, Akriti Prashar, Ana M. Pasapera, Katie Rollins, Eutteum Jeong, Rosa Puertollano
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The transcription factor TFE3 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. While its acute activation is cytoprotective, chronic TFE3 dysregulation is linked to diverse pathologies. Here, we characterize the cellular landscape of TFE3-NDD, a recently described neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations that disrupt the TFE3-Rag GTPase interface, leading to constitutive TFE3 nuclear localization. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, we show that TFE3-NDD is primarily a metabolic and homeostatic disorder. Mutant cells undergo a profound rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), resulting in metabolic rigidity and a vulnerability to energy failure. Despite a massive expansion of the lysosomal compartment, we observe a paradoxical qualitative failure characterized by impaired acidification, defective protease maturation, increased lysosomal exocytosis, and aberrant cathepsin K secretion. This secretory phenotype is coupled with a destabilized cell-extracellular matrix interface, marked by impaired migration, defective coordination between actomyosin tension and focal adhesion maturation, and a loss of synaptic stabilizers. Notably, TFE3-NDD shares a signature of high OXPHOS and ferroptosis resistance with TFE3-dependent cancers, such as translocation renal cell carcinoma. Our findings reveal how the chronic hyperactivation of a protective stress-response factor collapses cellular homeostasis, providing a mechanistic framework for the tissue malformations and neurodevelopmental deficits that define TFE3-NDD.

item.title: Temporal strain-resolved metagenomics associates IBD dysbiosis with gastrointestinal inflammation
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Ansorge
Stefano Romano
Clémence Frioux
Tamás Korcsmáros
Myeonghyun Yoou
Nathalie Juge
Katarzyna Sidorczuk
Falk Hildebrand
item.description:
Authors: Rebecca Ansorge, Stefano Romano, Clémence Frioux, Tamás Korcsmáros, Myeonghyun Yoou, Nathalie Juge, Katarzyna Sidorczuk, Falk Hildebrand
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is enriched in proinflammatory bacteria, yet defining a consistent dysbiotic signature is challenging, due to substantial variation between individuals and over time. We performed a high-resolution meta-analysis of 4,839 public metagenomes to disentangle the effects of IBD subtypes, inflammation, temporal, and individual variability. After accounting for temporal variation, we show that IBD-associated dysbiosis was characterized primarily by relative depletion of commensal bacteria rather than expansion of disease-associated taxa, together with increased microbiome variability both within and between individuals. Although 30% of species were IBD-associated, only 73% of these associations remained consistent across all timepoints. IBD-associated bacteria showed reduced persistence within hosts, increased strain loss and diminished strain engraftment. 8% of commensal species displayed strain-level associations with IBD that were independent of species-level changes, suggesting distinct ecological strategies for persistence. Finally, defining an inflammatory index, we demonstrated that inflammation explains much of the observed variation in microbial composition and abundance. Together, our findings indicate that inflammation associates and likely contributes to loss of commensals, thereby limiting microbiome recovery and resilience.

item.title: Strain-engineered fabrication of high-density aligned graphene-based nanoscrolls via UV-tunable adhesive tapes
item.dc:creator: Maki Nakatani
Akari Sudo
Pablo Solís-Fernández
Haiming Sun
Satoru Fukamachi
Tomoki Maezawa
Tatsuya Ikuta
Takako Matsunaga
item.description:
Authors: Maki Nakatani, Akari Sudo, Pablo Solís-Fernández, Haiming Sun, Satoru Fukamachi, Tomoki Maezawa, Tatsuya Ikuta, Takako Matsunaga, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10647
Abstract: Abstract Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. Although several methods have been proposed to synthesize GNSs, achieving high-density GNSs with controlled scroll chirality and direction remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the strain-engineered fabrication of large-scale GNSs using an ultraviolet (UV) light-tunable adhesive tape. The UV tape is stretched to apply tensile strain to graphene stacked on it, and releasing the applied strain by detaching the graphene from the tape results in the formation of GNSs. This strain-assisted method gives isolated GNSs of increased density ( ≈ 380 nanoscrolls per mm) and length (90 μm). This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. The nanoscroll structure allows the intercalation of metal chloride molecules, resulting in an increase of the electrical conductivity. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS 2 are realized by stretching MoS 2 /graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Our controlled synthesis of GNSs and heteronanoscrolls provides an opportunity to manipulate nanomaterials through the strain engineering with the functional UV tape.

item.title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
item.dc:creator: Chun-I Wu
Kalyan Banda
Rupali Arora

item.description:
Authors: Chun-I Wu, Kalyan Banda, Rupali Arora, T. Rinda Soong, Marc Radke, Melanie Dillon, Serena Nik-Zainal, Elizabeth M. Swisher, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10870
Abstract: Abstract Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

item.title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
item.dc:creator: Anjali P. Sapre
Melissa J. Martin
Ting L. Luo
Ulrike Carlino-MacDonald
Connor J. Davies
Emma G. Mills
Ana C. Ong
Rosslyn Maybank
item.description:
Authors: Anjali P. Sapre, Melissa J. Martin, Ting L. Luo, Ulrike Carlino-MacDonald, Connor J. Davies, Emma G. Mills, Ana C. Ong, Rosslyn Maybank, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The rise of Klebsiella pneumoniae combining antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes poses a major health threat, but the evolutionary routes and phenotypic consequences of this convergence are poorly understood. Here, phylogenetics of 1468 isolates and population analysis of 7520 plasmids, from >50 countries through the last two decades, reveal that convergence follows preferred, constrained evolutionary paths. The dominant route involves multidrug-resistant classical K. pneumoniae acquiring conjugative IncFIB(Mar)/IncHI1B(Mar) plasmids carrying an incomplete set of virulence biomarkers. Across 25 independent convergence events, the acquisition of the aerobactin siderophore locus was the only universal feature. These convergent isolates exhibit enhanced siderophore production but consistently lack the hypervirulent phenotype in vivo. In contrast, genuine hypervirulent strains that gain resistance remain rare. We conclude that enhanced siderophore production, not hypervirulence, is the primary adaptive trait driving the success of globally emerging convergent lineages, representing a distinct evolutionary state optimized for transmission rather than systemic invasion.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation – number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates – proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations.

Abstract: Abstract The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. Abstract: Abstract Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Due to the low efficiency of plant extraction and the high cost of semi-synthesis, efforts have been made to produce paclitaxel through biosynthesis. However, there have been no reports to date on engineered strains capable of paclitaxel biosynthesis. Here, we engineer a paclitaxel-producing line using the moss ( Physcomitrium patens ) chassis cells by combining transient expression verification, cytoplasmic localization strategies, self-cleaving 2 A peptide-mediated multi-gene co-expression systems and a modular iterative transformation strategy for stable genetic inheritance. Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10693
Abstract: Abstract Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum -infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. Twenty-three children were enroled; 20 were included in the primary analysis, across 10 cohorts. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

Abstract: Abstract The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. However, the capture efficiency of sequencing-based methods is generally low, which diminishes the effect of high capture resolution and negatively impacts subsequent data interpretation. Here, we introduce a spatial transcriptomic system, which provides ~1 μm capture resolution and a much higher capture efficiency. We demonstrate that as high as ~14,000 UMIs can be captured from mouse testis sample per 10 × 10 μm² area at a sequencing saturation of 0.43. Rare cells organized in single-cell-layers can be recovered when the data was analyzed at an effective resolution of 2 μm.

Authors: Jacob S. Roth, Joseph D. DeAngelo, Dejauwne L. Young, Maxim I. Maron, Kami Ahmad, Ankita Saha, Hugo Pinto, Varun Gupta, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO 2 and NO 3 – offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g g cat –1 h –1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

Abstract: Abstract Protein synthesis depends on specialized regulatory factors to overcome difficult-to-translate sequences during elongation that cause ribosomal stalling. In human mitochondria, this function is carried out by TACO1 (Translation activator of COX1). Using AlphaFold analysis and molecular dynamics simulations, we further show how a series of conformational changes allow its N-terminal domain to reorient and transiently engage with the A-site tRNA via a conserved and functionally critical basic amino acid patch. The bacterial homolog of TACO1, namely YebC2, shares the structural features required for its function. Overall, we present an evolutionarily conserved mechanism employed by TACO1 to enhance mitochondrial translation efficiency.

Abstract: Abstract Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. Abstract: Abstract Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae , including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. Abstract: Abstract Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

Abstract: Abstract Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. Abstract: Abstract Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. Abstract: Abstract Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10954
Abstract: Abstract High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

Abstract: Abstract Optical cavities enable strong, long-range, light-matter interactions that drive collective ordering, such as superradiant self-organization in ultracold atomic gases. We show that matching the grating periodicity to the enhanced electronic density fluctuations—such as those near Wigner crystallization—lowers the required pump intensity. Our results establish a route toward cavity-controlled electronic order in quantum materials.

Abstract: Abstract In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. item.description:
Authors: Sohyun Yim, Eun Hye Lee, Jungah Lee, Daeun Shin, Heekyoung Kang, Hee Kyung Park, Seonghyeon Kim, Joel B. Braunstein, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Plasma biomarkers that reflect distinct stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) could enable scalable biological staging. We evaluated phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species across multiple analytical platforms and the endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region containing residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) using a dedicated LC-MS/MS platform in a well-characterized cohort with amyloid PET and a subset with tau PET. While T1 biomarkers increased during preclinical stages, eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 increased later, consistent with fibrillar tau aggregation. eMTBR-tau243 showed the strongest and stage-dependent associations with regional tau PET and cognition, outperforming T1 biomarkers in predicting cross-sectional and longitudinal cognition. A plasma-based tau staging system integrating p-tau217 and eMTBR-tau243 closely aligned with PET-based tau staging and predicted longitudinal cognitive trajectories. These findings support plasma eMTBR-tau243 as a prototypical T2 biomarker and highlight the potential of plasma-based tau staging for prognosis and therapeutic decision-making in AD.

Authors: Rokas Petrenas, Katarzyna Ożga, Joel J. Chubb, Andrey V. Romanyuk, Dominic Alibhai, Jennifer J. McManus, Graham J. Leggett, Nigel S. Scrutton, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

item.description:
Authors: Yu Xiao, Ziyue Huang, Shihuai Wang, Xiaoyi Xu, Yu Cheng, Jingjing Guo, Ting He, Yang Liu, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. However, the phototherapeutic agents based on COFs are usually activated with ultraviolet and visible light, resulting in the limitation of deep-tissue phototherapy. Herein, we develop near-infrared-responsive COFs through elaborate design and synthesis of a thia-hexaphyrin building block, which feature well-aligned conjugation skeletons for the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photothermal effect upon 808 nm laser irradiation, outperforming conventional porphyrin-based COFs. This porous framework exhibits high phototherapeutic efficacy, leading to the tumor suppression for 4T1 tumors and CT26 tumors in female mouse model by inducing immunogenic cell death through phototherapy and triggering systemic anti-tumor immune responses.
